annotations.text:
VIEW 1 — Home / switcher (opened by the switcher chip in the editor top bar)
Absorbs the desktop landing page + tab bar. 'Documents' switches saved frameworks (open one marked). The switcher chip is the route back here, so it doubles as the home button.

VIEW 1 — 'New' tab = the type picker (desktop landing cards)
Choose the framework type for a new document; each type expands to examples + Create new + Generate. Real module names & descriptions.

VIEW 2 — Editor, Direction A (chosen)
Bottom command bar (final): Fit-to-view · Relayout | Evaluate | Export. UNDO moved to the top bar; REDO lives in the menu. Fit-to-view replaces desktop middle-click (no touch equivalent). Notifications show as a top-center toast (bottom is busy). Switcher chip = home; menu (top-right) = the long tail. Node gestures: double-tap canvas = add, tap = rename, hold = delete, hold+drag = attack.

VIEW 3 — Evaluate, one sheet for all kinds
Chip row = saved-config switcher: tap to switch, + adds a config (picks KIND only). Serialisation is a third kind (sequence output). The ⓘ by Semantics reveals a collapsible glossary definition + the entry's reference-paper link. Kind names are module-specific (ADF: interpretations).

VIEW 3 — Ranking folded in
Same chips, Categorizer active. Only the output differs: score chips + number badges on nodes; lattice semantics show an order a ≻ c ≻ b.

VIEW 4 — Export, format picker
Image formats open a preview (SVG now, PNG later); code/data formats download directly. Share-link kept as a separate one-tap action up top. Format list is per-module.

VIEW 4 — SVG preview, the one place config lives
Style options only affect the rendered image. Downloadable TikZ code is identical regardless; config just changes the \usepackage[...] line + the SVG.

BAF — attack vs support links
(1) Creation-mode selector pinned BOTTOM-LEFT of the canvas [Attack | Support] sets what a new edge will be. (2) Tapping an existing edge opens a type popover to switch attack↔support or delete. Support drawn as a double line.

iAF — uncertain arguments & attacks
Two stacked mode selectors BOTTOM-LEFT: Argument [solid ● | dashed ◌] and Attack [solid → | dashed ⇢] set the certainty of what you create next. Tapping an uncertain node offers Make definite / Delete (an edge uses the same popover as BAF).

ADF — acceptance condition editor
Tapping a node opens this sheet. Mobile keyboards lack ¬ ∧ ∨ ⊤ ⊥, so it carries an operator keypad + argument-atom chips that insert into the formula, with a live preview. Replaces the desktop floating condition bar.

PAF — probabilities
The desktop Probabilities window is a flat list, so it becomes a sheet: a slider + value per argument and attack. Entry point: in PAF the bottom bar carries an extra Probabilities button (right of Export); tapping a node jumps to its row.

TUTORIALS — overlay, never a separate screen
Docked card below the top bar; canvas + controls stay live underneath. Steps are button-advance (Next) or ACTION-advance — here it waits for a real tap, showing 'Waiting for you…' and spotlighting the target (Evaluate ringed, arrow pointing). Tutorials autostart, so no separate picker needed for now.

VIEW — Generate
Parameter form: algorithm select, sliders + numeric inputs, optional fixed seed, sticky Generate. Result shows stats + preview + Open in editor. Reached from the type picker's Generate and the menu.

VIEW — Glossary
Searchable, grouped list; each entry is title + definition + its reference-paper link (same reference data the eval ⓘ card surfaces). Opened from the menu.

MAIN MENU — the long tail (top-right hamburger)
Everything not on the bottom bar: document ops (New, Open file, Save, Generate), Redo + Share link, and app screens (Settings, Tutorials, Glossary, Help). A bottom sheet so it's thumb-reachable.

SETTINGS — from the menu
Every real setting: dark mode, graph style, physics default, show grid (off/on-drag/on), grid type, grid cell size, snap to grid, show tutorial hints. Physics & grid toggles live here (no bottom-bar buttons), matching your call.

RELAYOUT — sheet, two columns
The bottom-bar Relayout button opens this: Directed (Top→Bottom, Bottom→Top, Left→Right, Right→Left) and Other (Force-directed, Neato, Circular, Radial). All 8 desktop layouts, tap to apply.

HELP — gestures sheet (from the menu)
Rewritten for touch: double-tap = add, tap = rename, hold = delete, hold+drag = attack, drag/pinch = pan/zoom, fit-view = recenter, plus the bottom-left selector for BAF/iAF. Replaces the desktop mouse/keyboard controls overview.
